about: Donor families: a funder that publishes its own priorities, and the names under which its money appears in the filings. A pattern is a list of words that must all be in the contributor's name (or the committee's name) once upper-cased and stripped of punctuation. Families are listed most specific first; the first family whose pattern fits a name takes it. A person chose each pattern after reading the names the dataset holds (family_census in data/money_snapshot.json); the name as filed is kept on every row so a reader can disagree. 'link' says how the name ties to the organisation: the organisation's own treasury (own), a political committee the organisation runs (own committee), a committee that names the organisation as sponsor (sponsored committee), or only a name that looks alike (name only). 'committee_ids' lists FPPC ids that the Filers dataset resolves to a committee whose registered name states the family's name or sponsor (see data/money_snapshot.json, filers_lookup); a giver row carrying one of these ids belongs to the family whatever name the committee typed, which is how 'SF Forward' (no sponsor words) is read as the Chamber's committee.

families.name: San Francisco Chamber of Commerce
families.link_note: 'San Francisco Forward sponsored by San Francisco Chamber of Commerce' is a committee that names the Chamber as sponsor; the bare name 'SF Forward' carries no sponsor in the filing name.

families.name: Airbnb
families.link_note: The Airbnb money in these filings is a committee that names Airbnb as its supporter; no gift under Airbnb's own name was found.

families.name: Govern For California
families.link_note: The 'GFC Courage Committee' chapters are tied to Govern For California by the organisation's own pages, by press and by third-party records of the state filings, not by a registration read here. (1) Its 'Who We Are' page lists its independent political action committee chapters (Statewide, SF Public Schools, Southern California, Housing For Californians, San Francisco, Peninsula South Bay, East Bay) and its footer names 'Govern For California, a registered 501(c)(4) non-profit organization' (<https://www.governforcalifornia.org/who-we-are>, read 2026-10-30); its San Francisco voter guide says it was put together by 'GFC's San Francisco Chapter' (<https://www.governforcalifornia.org/news/2026/10/21/sf-voter-guide>). (2) Mission Local reported in 2024 that Govern for California gave $500 each to supervisor candidates through eight chapters, and that a complaint to the Ethics Commission alleged the payments came from one legal entity, which is an allegation and not a finding (<https://missionlocal.org/2024/09/s-f-ethics-complaint-targets-govern-for-california-group-that-bundles-political-donations/>). (3) Transparency USA's record of the state Govern for California Network Committee (id 1383984) lists payments to the San Francisco, Sierra, California Business Coalition, Palo Alto, Marin, Excellence in Education, Bay Area, Southern California and Golden Gate chapter committees (<https://www.transparencyusa.org/ca/committee/govern-for-california-network-committee-1383984-rcp>). (4) CalMatters' Digital Democracy lists chapter committee names, including Santa Cruz, Santa Barbara, Future Generations and Common Sense, under the organisation Govern for California (<https://calmatters.digitaldemocracy.org/organizations/-15028>). The chapter committees are state committees: the Ethics Commission's list of active committees for the 2 June 2026 election shows them as state-level committees with Cal-Access ids that match the ids on the filed rows (for example 1416440, the San Francisco chapter; <https://campaign.sfethics.org/elections/2026-06-02/committees/CA1433436>), but their Cal-Access registrations (Form 410), which name the sponsor, were not read, so the tie for each chapter rests on (1) to (4) and the name.
